dod_intent_evidence: DARPA SBIR Phase 2 for space-domain awareness — their own Space Intelligence page ('Our tech was built with DARPA to improve Space Domain Awareness detecting objects beyond the diffraction limit') plus Breaking Defense, 2026-01-13, and their own release announcing $4.2M pre-seed combined with a DARPA SBIR Phase 2 contract.
score_evidence: 'identify objects 20x further than any camera known to humanity' → lab_language_intensity: superlative benchmark claim with no platform, aperture, atmosphere or duty-cycle qualifier

'1000x faster in object detection and classification than conventional GPU/VPU + CMOS sensor ... 1000x more energy efficient than current GPU/VPUs, using photonic computing' → lab_language_intensity: three round-number multipliers as the entire product page

'winning first prize out of 1000 startups at SLUSH 2025 with a prize money of $1.2M, and winning $100k Best Space Innovation of 2025 at TechConnect' → lab_language_intensity: demo-circuit validation stands in for operational validation

Product page's only integration language is 'Output of the classification in USB-C, M8/M12 or other custom integrations' and 'Safely train your classification models directly in our cloud platform' — no rad-hard, TVAC, ITAR, IL4/IL5 or ATO anywhere → deployment_awareness_absence (capped at 12, own-language ~511 words)
No mention of an operator, analyst, ground-station crew, tasking workflow or field feedback anywhere in the pack → operator_absence (capped at 12)

Open roles are 'Head of Engineering', 'Software Engineer - Optical Simulation', 'Office Operations Manager' — a 14-person company still hiring its first engineering lead, with zero test, integration, space-qual or compliance roles → hiring_profile_skew
Founded 2025, pre-seed, '$4.2 million in combined pre-seed funding and a DARPA SBIR Phase 2 contract' → stage_pressure: Phase II period-of-performance clock against a constellation-scale ambition

blind_spots.blind_spot: The product's model-training and classification workflow is anchored to a company-run cloud, which is exactly the thing a DARPA SDA customer's network will not let them have.
blind_spots.operator_reality: The government analyst running space-domain awareness works on a classified enclave with no route to a startup's SaaS. Cloud-tethered training means the model can never be retrained on the customer's own data, and the sensor arrives as a black box the mission owner cannot update — the same failure as the 30fps crowd-detection case, but at the model-lifecycle layer rather than the bandwidth layer.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The team is a quantum-photonics spinout from MIT/UMD/Arizona shipping a commercial-style product page; nothing in the pack shows anyone who has taken a sensor through an IL5 enclave or an ATO.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Safely train your classification models directly in our cloud platform.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Every performance number is a bench comparison against CMOS/CCD with no environment attached — no thermal-vacuum, radiation, launch-vibration or on-orbit power-budget data for a photonic processor they intend to fly on a constellation.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A photonic computing unit on a smallsat bus lives in a -40C to +80C swing, total-ionizing-dose accumulation, and a bus that may allot tens of watts orbit-average. '1000x more energy efficient' means nothing to a program office until it is a watts-at-the-connector number with a TVAC and TID test report behind it, and that testing is measured in quarters — quarters the Phase II clock does not have.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Their only engineering hires are optical simulation and a not-yet-filled Head of Engineering; no environmental test, thermal, or spacecraft-integration engineer appears anywhere in the pack.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: 1000x more energy efficient than current GPU/VPUs, using photonic computing.

blind_spots.blind_spot: A university-spinout staffing model collides with export control on space-domain-awareness sensor data — deemed export is never mentioned despite roots in three research universities.
blind_spots.operator_reality: The moment SDA performance data becomes ITAR/EAR-controlled technical data, every non-US-person researcher on the team has to be walled off or licensed, and the company needs a technology control plan before it can take the next contract. Discovering that mid-Phase-II costs months and can force staff off the program that built the technology.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The company presents itself through academic lineage and prize wins rather than as a defense contractor; there is no compliance, security, or contracts function visible and no ITAR/CMMC/NIST 800-171 language on the site.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Our startup has roots in MIT, University of Maryland, and University of Arizona.

opener_hook: Your product page offers model training 'directly in our cloud platform' while your DARPA Phase 2 is for space-domain awareness — those two live on networks that never touch, and the reconciliation usually eats a quarter no one budgeted.
what_they_do: MIT/University of Maryland spinout building a quantum camera and photonic processing unit that images past the optical diffraction limit, aimed at satellite constellations for space-domain awareness and Earth intelligence.
